§7.2.9 Quote Blocks

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-quote-blocks · text formatting

✅ Normative

A quoted or inset region MUST be flattened: its content is rendered as ordinary text, headings and tables included. The output MUST NOT add > block-quote markers.

A boxed or inset region on the page renders as:

## here we go
Yeah

not:

>
> ## here we go
> Yeah

Why flatten

Block-quote markers interact badly with headings and tables that sit inside the quoted region. Most inset regions in real documents are not quotations at all — they are callouts, pull quotes or sidebars that happen to be visually offset. Flattening keeps the content addressable. The cost is losing the "this was inset" signal, and that cost is accepted.

A real quotation

In prose documents an inset block sometimes does mean someone else said this. It is flattened all the same: the words survive, and every printed character of them — quotation marks, attribution line — MUST be kept.
